text:
**Best pick: [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).** It has a **2,600 W inverter** and **2,073.6 Wh battery**, giving it headroom for a typical 1,800 W single-burner induction cooktop. At full power, expect roughly **an hour of continuous cooking**; actual meal time can be longer if you turn the heat down. ([Specs and estimates](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))

For a kettle, check its wattage label: the station’s AC output needs to meet or exceed that rating. A kettle uses energy for a relatively short time—boiling a litre is roughly **90–110 Wh**—so battery capacity matters less than having enough inverter output. ([Boil estimates](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))

The **BLUETTI AC180** and **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** are also listed at 1,800 W output, but that’s right at the stated requirement for a full-power induction burner, with less headroom. ([Comparison](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))
